title: Reasons To Start Buying Bonds
gist: In a paywalled teaser, Gavekal's Anatole Kaletsky breaks with colleagues and says it is finally time to buy government bonds, five years into the worst bond bear market since the 1970s. He still holds that the 2022 inflationary regime change will keep rates higher for years or decades, so his call is a tactical or valuation-based reversal, not a change of regime view. The reasoning is not in the teaser.

insights.claim: Government bonds are in their fifth year of the worst bear market since the 1970s, and one senior Gavekal strategist now argues it is time to start buying them.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: A long-standing G7 bond bear turning bullish on valuation is a possible capitulation signal, but the argument is behind the paywall and cannot be assessed here.
insights.quote: Five years into the worst bear market in government bonds since the 1970s, is it finally time to buy bonds?
insights.locator: Five years into the worst bear market

insights.claim: The bullish bond call is reached without abandoning the higher-rates regime view. The author still believes the 2022 regime change forces interest rates higher for years or even decades, which implies the case for buying rests on something other than falling inflation or rates.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Look for a case based on starting yields, valuation or relative value rather than a rate-cut cycle. This is an inference, since the teaser does not give the argument.
insights.locator: Why then do I now disagree with Charles

insights.claim: The author has urged investors to avoid all G7 bond markets since early 2022. He attributes a once-in-a-lifetime global regime change toward a more inflationary environment to the combination of the Ukraine war and Covid.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: The author's bond bear thesis was regime-based, so a reversal from him is a bigger signal than a cyclical call would be.
insights.quote: a once-in-a-lifetime global “regime change” towards a more inflationary environment that is bound to force interest rates higher for years or even decades ahead
insights.locator: In contrast to most of my colleagues

insights.claim: Most of the author's Gavekal colleagues remain bearish or neutral on bonds. Charles is unequivocally bearish on US, UK and French bonds, and Will sees US long bonds as unattractive or at best neutral on underlying economic value.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: The house view is split, so the consensus among bond bears is not uniform. US, UK and French bonds are singled out as the bearish targets.
insights.quote: Charles, who remains unequivocally bearish about the US, UK and French bond markets
insights.locator: Why then do I now disagree with Charles
